answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and stands that Player ID card visibly in front of them. They take the Voting card set matching that color on its backs, remove cards targeting colors not in the game, and keep their own Ambush card. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: choose a color and stand its Player ID card visibly; remove cards targeting colors not playing; deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, keeping values hidden.

answers.answer: There is no individual player-by-player turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed” and “reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is necessary. The Target is the player or players receiving the most votes; Red's three votes exceed Blue's and Green's two each, so Red is the sole Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and can survive, unless some other elimination rule applies.
answers.evidence: Vote: tied players are all Targets; Targets are eliminated unless protected by their own successful Ambush. With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.”

answers.answer: Ambush cards do not count as votes. Based on the stated votes, Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow give Red and Yellow one vote each, tying them as Targets. Red is a Target and successfully Ambushes, so Red survives and may eliminate one player who voted for Red; Yellow is the only such voter, so Red may eliminate Yellow. Pink voted for a Target (Yellow), so Pink satisfies the voting requirement and survives. The summary does not specify any other players' votes or outcomes.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Ambush cards do not count as votes”; tied players are all Targets; voting for any tied Target satisfies the requirement. Ambush: a Target's successful Ambush survives and eliminates one player who voted for them.

answers.answer: No. The successful ambusher chooses only one player who voted for them, even if four players did so. They cannot choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: a successful ambusher “chooses one of the players who voted for them” and “cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: The player eliminates themselves. An Ambush works only if its player is a Target; if the player is not a Target, the Ambush fails and they eliminate themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded at four survivors. The players continue with another conspiracy and vote among the four surviving players; only survivors participate in subsequent votes.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: with three or more survivors, “Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are not four points: each is a card worth 3, 4, or 5 points, and the values are hidden when the central pot is dealt.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: one survivor collects “all four central Gold Bars.” Components: each bar is a card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Final Showdown cards. They may discuss a bargain, then each secretly selects one card; both reveal their choices simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes a set of cards; they may discuss a bargain, then each secretly selects one card and they reveal both simultaneously.

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive no bar from this no-survivor reward. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: with no survivors, each player “not participating in the final vote” receives one bar from the deck; leave the four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share finalist receives zero central bars and the Steal finalist receives all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: Share player gets 0; Steal player gets 4.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist receives one central bar and the Steal finalist receives three central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: Grab One & Go player gets 1; Steal player gets 3.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist receives one central bar and the Share finalist receives three central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Share: Grab One & Go player gets 1; Share player gets 3.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar, leaving two in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars for the next round.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Grab One & Go, each receives one central bar, two remain in the center, and “add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: if both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold; every other player gets one bar from the deck; leave all four central bars for next round and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: check at the end of a round after bars are awarded; thresholds are 25 points for 6–9 players and 24 for 10–12; if multiple qualify, the highest point total wins.

answers.answer: If exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total, those tied players conduct another Final Showdown; continue until a single player at the table has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated earlier in that round, and all Player ID cards are stood upright for the next round.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: tied players conduct another Final Showdown, continuing until a single player has the highest total. Turn Structure: if there is no winner, everyone returns; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
